surface_mechanism_description: The exchange reaction between bismuth chloride and water could nominally result in the formation of bismuth oxide. Bismuth oxide, Bi2O3, has several equally strong reflections in its powder X-ray pattern (Card 029-0236), among which 223 and 621 at 54.3 and 55.5°, respectively, might overlap with the broad intense peak in the observed pattern (Fig. 1). However, in accord with the XRF analysis, the film deposited contained also considerable amounts of residual chlorine. It is known that, whenever chlorine or chloride is present in a system aiming at the production of bismuth oxides, rather stable bismuth oxide chloride, BiOCl, tends to form.
